evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits this theorem through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate, which re-checks the proof term against the stated type, so producing this row at all is a machine-checked proof. The proof term is `le_succ (mul 2 n)` -- the already-proved generic lemma `m <= succ m` instantiated at `m := mul 2 n` -- accepted directly by the kernel's definitional-equality check, because `bit false n` unfolds to `mul 2 n` and `bit true n` unfolds to `succ (mul 2 n)` (delta+iota, per `F:nat-bit-false`/`F:nat-bit-true`). evidence.supports: bit(false, n) <= bit(true, n), for every n

formal.statement: theorem Nat.bit_false_le_bit_true : ((x0 : AxNat) -> AxNat.le (AxNat.bit Bool.false x0) (AxNat.bit Bool.true x0))

notes:
formal.statement is `Kernel::render_lean` of the admitted type, taken verbatim from `nat_theorem_inventory`, not transcribed by hand. `AxNat` is the kernel's CONSTRUCTED inductive `Nat` (the `Ax` is *axeyum*, not *axiomatized*) -- the `nat` prelude's trusted surface measures zero.

Like `F:nat-bit-true-pos`, this is a defeq corollary bought by `nat_prelude/bits.rs`'s `add`-outermost construction: both `bit false n` and `bit true n` unfold to the SAME two terms (`mul 2 n` and `succ (mul 2 n)`) an already-proved generic order lemma (`le_succ`) already relates, so no new case-split machinery was needed. This is not itself the `F:ml430-*` Mathlib mirror family (those all name `Nat.bitwise`/`Nat.land`/`Nat.lor`/`Nat.ldiff`, none of which this lane declares); it is a genuinely new fact about this prelude's own `Nat.bit`.
statement: For every n, appending bit `false` to n's little end is at most appending bit `true`.
title: bit(false, n) <= bit(true, n)
